Objectives:
The Little Creek Mtn grazing allotment has received several
vegetative treatment projects over the last 30 years. Recently,
1100 acres of previously chained and seeded areas were treated with
herbicide to control the reestablishment of shrubs and trees .
The herbicide treatment is currently achieving the desired
objective of removing shrubs allowing the grasses and forbs (native
and seeded) to thicken and expand .
Another approx. . 700 acres have been identified for herbicide
treatment in this same area. Areas were identified based on the
existence of adequate grass and forbs to respond to treatment and
the occurrence of establishing shrubs and/or trees which are
competing with the desired species.
If maintenance is not completed the shrubs and trees will continue
to gain dominance reducing the amount of grass and forbs . This has
been a beneficial project currently producing livestock forage and
improving forage diversity for deer and other wildlife.
Application of tebuthiuron should extend the life of the initial
investment on the 700 acres by another 25 to 30 years.
Planned_Implementation:
Approximately 700 acres of existing chained areas will be
maintained by aerial application of tebuthiuron. The rate will be
0. 8 lbs active ingredient per acre on approximately 100 acres
where sagebrush and pinyon/juniper control is needed while the
remaining acreage will be treated at 0.5 lbs per acre to control
sagebrush. Application rates were determined based on the success
of the previously treated 1100 acres and other nearby projects.

fixed-wing flight patterns for spraying. The many small draws in the northern
portion are not conducive to good fixed wing spraying. If this type of
blocking is accomplished, leaving sagebrush in the upper portions of the
draws, the sage grouse population in that area should not be adversely
affected. If the decision is made to use a helicopter for the job, two or
three of the smaller draws having the smallest sage composition should be
left for sage grouse habitat. Those draws containing grassy meadows
and/or water will be most beneficial to sage grouse.
